0.headline: Telecom InvITs may offer investors a new path to bet on India’s 5G data boom
0.heading: Telecom InvITs may offer investors a new path to bet on India’s 5G data boom
0.intro: The upcoming Altius offering could open a more defensive, income-oriented route into telecom infrastructure, though analysts caution that predictable distributions come with lower growth potential and customer-concentration risks
0.body:
Brookfield-backed Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust’s proposed public offering could give investors a new way to participate in the country’s rising data consumption and 5G rollout without directly betting on a telecom operator.

Altius, which filed draft documents with the Securities and Exchange Board of India on August 6, operates around 2.58 lakh telecom sites, supporting around 3.15 lakh tenancies.

Until now, public-market investors seeking exposure to India’s telecom growth have largely had to choose between telecom operators such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea or tower-company stocks such as Indus Towers.

Steady gains

A publicly listed telecom InvIT would add a more yield-focused option built around rental income from operating infrastructure assets.

“Telecom InvITs offer a more defensive, income-oriented way to participate in India’s digital infrastructure growth,” Equirus Capital managing director Vijay Agrawal said.

Returns from telecom operators depend on subscriber growth, average revenue per user, spectrum costs, network expenditure, competition and regulation, he said. This creates greater volatility but also higher potential returns if tariffs, average revenue per user (ARPU) and market share improve.

“In contrast, telecom InvITs earn contracted rentals or infrastructure-provisioning fees under long-term agreements with escalations, supporting visible cash flows and regular distributions,” Agrawal said.

InvITs are also required to distribute at least 90 percent of their net distributable cash flows to unitholders. This makes the sustainability of distributions rather than maximising earnings growth central to the investment proposition.

“InvITs do offer a better route for investors who primarily prefer predictable cash-flow generation instead of maximum upside,” Anand Rathi Investment Banking director Vipin Singhal said.

Singhal said telecom towers function as shared utility assets. As data traffic rises, infrastructure providers can benefit from additional rentals, equipment upgrades and network expansion without bearing the entire commercial risk of selling telecom services to end-consumers.

The three available investment routes consequently occupy different positions on the risk-return spectrum.

“Telecom operator offers the highest growth upside with volatile earnings and high capex intensity along with aggressive tariff competition,” Singhal said.

Tower companies occupy the middle ground, with recurring infrastructure revenue but greater operating flexibility over expansion, capital allocation and dividends.

Agrawal described Altius as a predictable-yield platform, compared with Indus Towers, which could be treated more as a growth platform.

The sector’s underlying growth outlook remains supportive. India had 430 million 5G subscriptions at the end of 2025, according to Ericsson, which expects the number to exceed 1.1 billion by 2031. Average monthly data usage per smartphone is forecast to increase from 37 GB to 70 GB over this period.

Telecom InvITs may therefore be better suited to investors seeking regular income and infrastructure-linked yields rather than aggressive capital appreciation.

To be sure, growth is not entirely absent.

“Growth can come from contractual escalations, additional tenancies, new deployments, operational efficiencies and accretive acquisitions, although acquisitions may require debt or equity and do not automatically create value,” Agrawal said.

The biggest concern, however, is that India’s telecom market is dominated by a small number of operators. Financial stress, delayed payments, consolidation, tenancy exits or contract renegotiations could affect cash flows and distributions. Investors must also consider leverage, refinancing costs, debt-funded acquisitions, regulatory changes and slower-than-expected network rollouts.

“The primary risk is customer concentration,” Agrawal said, adding, “rising data consumption and 5G adoption are supportive but do not eliminate these risks.”

Singhal added that telecom InvITs should not be viewed as a substitute for telecom stocks.

The distinction investors need to make is between a yield-oriented infrastructure investment offering relatively predictable income and a higher-risk equity bet carrying potentially greater growth.

1.headline: Shankesh Jewellers IPO subscribed nearly 3x on Day 3; check latest GMP
1.heading: Shankesh Jewellers IPO subscribed nearly 3x on Day 3; check latest GMP
1.intro: The initial public offering (IPO) of Shankesh Jewellers witnessed a pick-up in investor interest on the third and final day of bidding, with the issue receiving 2.8 times subscription by 5:00 pm on August 20, according to data from the NSE.
1.body:
The initial public offering (IPO) of Shankesh Jewellers witnessed a pick-up in investor interest on the third and final day of bidding, with the issue receiving 2.8 times subscription by 5:00 pm on August 20, according to data from the NSE.

The issue received bids for 7,74,20,480 equity shares against 2,76,37,400 shares offered for subscription. Non-institutional investors led the demand with 5.68 times subscription, followed by retail investors with 2.42 times subscription.

The Rs 367.18-crore IPO opened for subscription on August 18 and closes on August 20. The company has fixed the price band at Rs 88-93 per equity share. At the upper end of the price band, the company is valued at around Rs 1,367 crore. The minimum lot size is 160 shares, requiring an investment of Rs 14,880 at the upper price band.

Read Also: Tempsens Instruments IPO subscribed 42% so far on Day 1; GMP surges to 73%

In the grey market, the premium for Shankesh Jewellers shares has eased from earlier levels. Investorgain reported the latest grey market premium (GMP) at Rs 2.5 per share as of 9:53 am on August 20. At the upper IPO price of Rs 93, this indicates an estimated listing price of around Rs 95.5, or a potential premium of about 2.7 percent.

IPO Watch, meanwhile, reported a GMP of Rs 2 as of 8:30 am on August 20, implying an estimated gain of 2.15 percent over the upper price band. The platform had reported a GMP of Rs 5 on August 19.

Grey market premiums are unofficial indicators and can change before listing. They do not guarantee the actual listing price or returns.

Ahead of the public issue, Shankesh Jewellers raised Rs 110.15 crore from anchor investors at Rs 93 per share, the upper end of the IPO price band. The company allocated more than 1.18 crore shares to 14 anchor investors.

The anchor allocation included Tiger Strategies Fund-I, Necta Bloom VCC, Venus Investment VCC, Zeal Global Opportunities Fund, ASAS Global Fund and Uni Growth Fund. The allocation did not include domestic mutual funds, life insurance companies or pension funds.

Check IPO News Here

The IPO comprises a fresh issue of around Rs 274.18 crore and an offer for sale of up to 1 crore equity shares worth around Rs 93 crore. The fresh issue proceeds will be used towards repayment or pre-payment of borrowings, working capital requirements and general corporate purposes.

The equity shares are scheduled to list on the BSE and NSE on August 25. The basis of allotment is expected to be finalised on August 21, followed by refunds and credit of shares on August 24.

About Shankesh Jewellers

Shankesh Jewellers, a Mumbai-based B2B jewellery company, manufactures handcrafted 22-karat and 18-karat gold jewellery and supplies products to corporate and non-corporate clients across India. Its clients include Joyalukkas India, P N Gadgil &amp; Sons, Kalyan Jewellers India and Novel Jewels, among others.

2.headline: Annu Projects sets price band at Rs 94-99 per share, IPO to hit Dalal Street on August 25
2.heading: Annu Projects sets price band at Rs 94-99 per share, IPO to hit Dalal Street on August 25
2.intro: Annu Projects IPO | The company is raising Rs 175.06 crore through an initial public offering of 1.76 crore equity shares, comprising an entirely fresh issue.
2.body:
Annu Projects, the EPC company focused on fibre optics, sewerage and gas pipeline projects, on August 20 fixed the price band at Rs 94-99 per share for its upcoming IPO.

The company is raising Rs 175.06 crore through an initial public offering (IPO) of 1.76 crore equity shares, comprising an entirely fresh issue, and is seeking a market capitalisation of Rs 648 crore at the upper end of the price band.

The IPO will open for public subscription on August 25 and close on August 28.

Investors can bid for a minimum of 151 equity shares and in multiples of 151 shares thereafter. Accordingly, the minimum investment for retail investors would be Rs 14,949, while the maximum would be Rs 1,94,337.

Annu Projects has reserved 50 percent of the IPO shares for retail investors, while 40 percent of the shares are allocated to non-institutional investors and the remaining 10 percent of the issue size is reserved for qualified institutional buyers.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

The company, which competes with listed peers such as Likhitha Infrastructure, Bondada Engineering, EMS and Suyog Telematics, will spend Rs 15.4 crore of the net issue proceeds on the purchase of machinery and equipment. Further, up to Rs 115 crore will be utilised for working capital requirements, while the remaining funds will be used for general corporate purposes.

The New Delhi-based EPC company provides essential overhead and underground utilities infrastructure services across the telecom, sewerage and gas pipeline verticals, which contributed 41.5 percent, 52.7 percent and 4 percent, respectively, to its FY26 topline.

Annu Projects reported a standalone profit of Rs 33 crore and revenue of Rs 241.2 crore for the fiscal year ended March 2026.

Mefcom Capital Markets is acting as the sole book-running lead manager for the Annu Projects IPO.
